Dear Wanderer,
Some time ago, this old man accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the local school. There, I saw the children sitting upright and engrossed in their books, so absorbed that they didn’t even notice our approach.
Curious, I wondered what marvelous texts could captivate these usually restless youngsters so completely. Upon asking, I learned that they were reading books you had gifted them not long ago.
When I inquired what made these books so special, the children eagerly chimed in, and I realized you had thoughtfully chosen different books for each child. Hearing that I knew you, they begged me to convey their gratitude.
Yet, when pressed to express their thanks aloud, they grew shy and tongue-tied. So, I suggested they write down their thoughts, which I’ve enclosed here—unread, I assure you!
They also entrusted me with a few drawings, inspired by the books you gave. They insisted you, with your discerning taste, would appreciate their masterpieces.
Ha Ha, it seems any future tasks involving children should undoubtedly be entrusted to you, Wanderer.
